name: Paraguay
summary: Red, white and blue horizontal bands with a different emblem on each side: the national arms on the front and the treasury seal on the back. It is one of only a few national flags whose two sides differ.
origin: Paraguay declared independence from Spain in 1811. Red, white and blue were used from the early years; the colours are often linked to the French tricolour or to the flags of the Río de la Plata.
The current design, with different emblems on each side, was set by Congress on 25 November 1842. The emblems were redrawn several times, most recently in 2013.

symbols.name: Coat of arms (obverse)
symbols.description: A yellow five-pointed star (the Star of May) in a wreath of palm and olive, with 'República del Paraguay' around it.

symbols.name: Treasury seal (reverse)
symbols.description: A lion beside a pole topped by a red Phrygian cap, with the motto 'Paz y Justicia' (Peace and Justice).
symbols.meaning: The lion defends liberty, symbolised by the cap.

facts: Paraguay's flag is one of very few national flags with different designs on each side; the flag of Saudi Arabia is double-sided but identical.
Its lion and Phrygian cap echo French revolutionary symbolism.
clues: Red, white and blue horizontal bands with a different emblem on each side.
Its reverse shows a lion guarding a liberty cap.
Its front shows a star named after the month of its independence.
